ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $AB=3$, $AC=4$. $D$, $E$, and $F$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$, $BC$, and $AC$ respectively. Connect $DE$, $DF$, and $EF$, with the measure of $\angle ADF$ being $53^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $D$ and $F$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AC$ respectively, \\
$\therefore DF \parallel BC$, \\
Since $\angle ADF = 53^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle B = \angle ADF = 53^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle A = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle C = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 53^\circ = \boxed{37^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, point A of triangle ABC is above, point B is at the lower left, and point C is at the lower right; D is on side AB, F is on side AC, E is on side BC, and DE, DF, and EF are connected in the figure, where DF is the line segment connecting two points on AB and AC, and it appears to be parallel to the base BC. Reasoning: The problem gives that D and F are the midpoints of AB and AC respectively, so by the triangle midline theorem, DF ∥ BC. Because AD and AB are on the same straight line, and DF ∥ BC, ∠ADF is equal to ∠ABC, that is, ∠B = 53°. Also because ∠A = 90°, and the sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°, ∠C = 180° − 90° − 53° = 37°.
